customManagers.description: Versions in a Dockerfile `ARG` carrying a renovate comment, e.g. `# renovate: datasource=crate depName=cargo-chef` followed by `ARG CARGO_CHEF_VERSION=0.1.78`

Runner labels in a workflow matrix, e.g. `runner: ubuntu-26.04-arm` in `build.yaml`: the `github-actions` manager reads `runs-on` only, so these would stay on the old image. Same depName as the `runs-on` labels, so both land in one PR
Images a shell script runs, pinned in a variable under a renovate comment

packageRules.description: Commit subjects follow the repository's lowercase imperative style, e.g. `deps: bump regex to v1.13.2`. Set here rather than at the top level, where manager defaults would win
Minor and patch bumps land as one PR; each major gets its own
Below 1.0 a minor bump is a breaking release, e.g. reqwest 0.12 to 0.13: it gets its own PR rather than breaking the group
The SDK and exporters only compile against the matching opentelemetry release: bumped one at a time, each PR fails to build

`@astrojs/markdown-satteri` pins the `satteri` it runs plugins with, and `astro` and Starlight pin `@astrojs/markdown-satteri`: bumped alone, the config's mdast plugin is typed against a second `satteri` and fails
The Rust toolchain `mise.toml` pins and the Dockerfile's `rust` builder image stay on one version
The hadolint hook runs the `hadolint` binary `mise.toml` pins: the hook revision and the binary stay on one release
trivy-action runs its default Trivy, which is the one `mise.toml` pins for the pre-commit hook: one Trivy, one ruleset
The config validator hook and the Renovate image the workflow runs come from the same Renovate release

TypeScript stays on 6: `astro check` (`@astrojs/check`, peer `typescript ^5 || ^6`) refuses TypeScript 7.0, see https://github.com/withastro/astro/issues/17268. Lift once `@astrojs/check` accepts TypeScript 7, or once TypeScript 7.1 is stable with a non-experimental `@astrojs/ts-content-mapper` to replace `astro check`
